sovereign_country.strategic_role: 拉美美元金融中枢、私人利益基金会（PIF）与运河船舶登记

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Motion Picture International Copyright Distribution and Licensing

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid (Codified civil law system with strong Anglo-American commercial and corporate law influence, notably Law 32 of 1927 for corporations and Law 25 of 1995 for Private Interest Foundations)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: United States-Panama Trade Promotion Agreement (investment chapter; in force 2012)
Panama-Mexico Bilateral Investment Treaty and Double Taxation Agreement (active)
Panama-South Korea Free Trade and Investment Promotion Agreement (in force 2021)
Panama-United Arab Emirates Double Taxation Agreement (active)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law No. 23 of 27 April 2015 (AML/CFT framework), as amended by Law No. 70 of 2019 and Law No. 129 of 2020; Law No. 25 of 12 June 1995 (Private Interest Foundation Law), as amended; Law No. 52 of 27 August 2016 (final beneficiary registry and due-diligence rules for obliged subjects); Law No. 129 of 17 March 2020 (beneficial-owner identification and confidentiality regime for Private Interest Foundations); implementing rules and resolutions of the Superintendencia de Sujetos No Financieros (SSNF) and binding instructions of the Unidad de Analisis Financiero (UAF). The statutory UBO ownership threshold is 10% of capital or voting rights for equity-based entities; for a Private Interest Foundation the duty is role-based and identifies the founder, foundation council members, beneficiaries, protector and any natural person exercising ultimate control, irrespective of percentage.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized Foundation Charter and Bylaws (Escritura Publica Constitutiva and Estatutos de la Fundacion de Interes Privado)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Panamanian Notary Public (Notaria del Circuito de Panama)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Domestic notarization followed by inscription at the Registro Publico de Panama; apostille not required for domestic use

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Founder's notarized passport or national identity document (if individual founder)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary or civil registrar in the founder's country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (if country is party to the 1961 Hague Convention) or Consular Legalization by a Panama consulate

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing or Certificate of Incumbency of the founder (if corporate founder) and corporate authority resolutions authorizing the foundation's creation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporate registry or equivalent competent authority of the founder's country of incorporation

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter for the founder and the proposed foundation council members
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Issuing bank or reputable financial institution
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization plus apostille or consular legalization in accordance with the origin jurisdiction's standards

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Power of Attorney (if the foundation is constituted by a legal representative) together with the representative's certified passport copy
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public of the grantor's jurisdiction

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Ley No. 25 de 12 de junio de 1995 (Private Interest Foundation Act), as amended by Ley No. 41 de 2013; Articles 5-7 (Foundation Charter, endowment, and contents) and Articles 20-21 (Foundation Council); registration rules of the Registro Público de Panamá.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registro Público de Panamá — Dirección General de Registro (Mercantile and Documents Section), Panama City, Republic of Panama
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Escritura Pública de Fundación de Interés Privado (notarized Foundation Charter) presented for inscription (Inscripción)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Statutory minimum foundation endowment of USD 10,000 (Law 25 of 1995, Article 7), declared in the Foundation Charter. The endowment may be contributed in cash, securities, or other assets; no escrow account is statutorily required, and the capital must be sufficient for the foundation's stated purpose.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: WE, the undersigned, being the designated Foundation Council members of PA_PIF, hereby RESOLVE as follows: (1) The initial endowment of USD 10,000 declared in the Foundation Charter is accepted and recorded as the founding capital of the Foundation. (2) The registered office at Panama City, Republic of Panama, is adopted as the statutory domicile, and the licensed Resident Agent is ratified. (3) [Name] is appointed President, [Name] Secretary, and [Name] Treasurer of the Foundation Council. (4) The officers are jointly and severally authorized to open bank accounts, execute motion-picture licensing agreements, appoint correspondents, and perform all acts necessary to implement the Foundation's statutory objectives. This Resolution is effective upon adoption and shall be recorded in the Foundation Protocol.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Engage licensed Panamanian Resident Agent and draft Foundation Charter
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed Panamanian attorney or fiduciary company (Agente Residente); pre-review by the Registro Público de Panamá name-search office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Instruct the Resident Agent to draft the Spanish-language Foundation Charter (Estatutos) containing the foundation's name, purpose (ISIC 5911 independent motion-picture copyright distribution and licensing), minimum endowment of USD 10,000, registered office address, Foundation Council members, beneficiaries and protector (optional), and amendment/duration provisions. Verify name availability through the Public Registry's official search before execution.
required_dossiers: Passport or valid ID of founder
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the proposed name is rejected for conflict, submit two alternative names for expedited re-search; if drafting defects are detected, the Resident Agent amends and re-presents the draft within five working days at no additional statutory cost.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execute and notarize the Foundation Charter before a Panamanian Notary
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notaría Pública de Panamá (Public Notary) in Panama City
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The founder appears before the notary, executes the Foundation Charter, and the notary incorporates the act into his or her protocol, verifying identity, capacity, and the mandatory contents under Articles 5-6 of Law 25 of 1995. The original charter is converted into an Escritura Pública with notarial seal and certified copies are produced for registry filing.
required_dossiers: Founder's passport or corporate certification if the founder is an entity
Notarized and legalized power of attorney if the founder acts through counsel
Endowment declaration or asset valuation statement
Resident Agent designation and acceptance document
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary issues observations, the founder executes a corrective amendment deed (corrección) or re-executes the charter; any notarial fee variance is settled with the notary and the registry copy is re-issued within three working days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: File the notarized charter with the Public Registry for inscription
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá — Dirección General de Registro (Mercantile and Documents Section)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the certified copy of the Escritura Pública together with the filing petition, receipt of fee payment, and the Resident Agent's acceptance. The Registry's legal reviewer verifies compliance with Law 25 of 1995, clears any name or formal objections, and, upon approval, grants the inscription by which the Foundation acquires legal personality.
required_dossiers: Certified copy of the notarized Escritura Pública (three signed copies)
Proof of payment of registry and stamp fees
Copy of the Resident Agent's professional license
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar issues an objection (observación), the defect must be cured within the stated term (generally ten working days) by filing a corrective notarial deed; an appeal may be lodged with the Dirección General of the Public Registry, and failure to cure requires a new filing with corresponding fees.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Pay registration fees and obtain the registered charter excerpt
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá — Tesorería and Certification Office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Settle the inscription fee (approximately USD 250), stamp duties, and the first annual franchise tax at the Registry's treasury; thereafter collect the registered copy (copia registrada) and the inscription certification evidencing legal personality and publication of the foundation's existence.
required_dossiers: Certified copy of the inscribed charter
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the treasury rejects or recalculates the fee, obtain a corrected collection receipt (constancia de pago) and reconcile the amount against the official fee schedule; disputed charges may be appealed to the Registry's internal administrative review within five working days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Hold the constituent Foundation Council meeting and open the Foundation Protocol
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Foundation Council and the Resident Agent's registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the first Foundation Council meeting at the registered office, adopt the First Board Resolution covering acceptance of the endowment, adoption of the registered office, and appointment of officers, and record the act in the Foundation Protocol (Protocolo) together with the opening entries of the statutory books (book of acts and book of accounts), which must be legalized by the notary.
required_dossiers: Officer appointment acceptance letters (cargos de aceptación)
Protocol opening entry with notarial legalization
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a designated officer declines appointment, the Council adopts a corrective resolution appointing a substitute; if the minutes are inconsistent with the Charter, the Council rectifies the minutes by a subsequent act and re-records them chronologically in the Protocol.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Finalize tax and municipal registrations for operational readiness
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) of the Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas; Municipio de Panama; CSS if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Obtain the Foundation's RUC tax identification with DGI, file any required information returns, and, if a physical office is established, apply for the municipal Aviso de Operación with the Municipality of Panama and register with the CSS social security system if staff are hired; preserve the non-resident or territorial-source status for the licensing revenue model.
required_dossiers: Declaration of no Panamanian-source income (where applicable)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If DGI or the municipality queries the application, correct the supporting charter excerpt and re-submit; zoning objections are cured by lease amendments or relocation, and appealed to the municipal review board within the statutory objection window.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable for film copyright distribution and licensing (no national sectoral license required); reference body: Ministerio de Comercio e Industrias (MICI) and the Panama Film Commission (Comisión Fílmica de Panamá) for voluntary promotional registration only
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Exempt — no operating or manufacturing permit required for ISIC 5911 copyright licensing activities; optional municipal Aviso de Operación for physical office premises

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministerio de Ambiente de Panamá (MiAMBIENTE) — Dirección de Verificación del Desempeño Ambiental
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category I (Environmental Registration) — low-impact office-based licensing and distribution activities; a full EIA study is not required under Law 41 of 1998 and Decreto Ejecutivo 123 de 2009; only an Environmental Performance Registration form is filed
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial point-source discharges: office sanitary wastewater must meet MiAMBIENTE municipal sewer discharge thresholds (pH 6.0-9.0; BOD5 not exceeding 200 mg/L; TSS not exceeding 220 mg/L); solid waste disposed under national waste-stream regulations; no VOC or noise emission thresholds triggered by office licensing operations

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire-safety inspection and operating certificate from the Benemérito Cuerpo de Bomberos de Panamá; municipal structural load and occupancy inspection for the registered office; occupational health and safety clearance from the Ministerio de Trabajo y Desarrollo Laboral (MITRADEL) including workplace risk signage and evacuation plans

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) of the Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas (MEF); operational e-filing and e-invoicing portal: SITe (Sistema Integrado de Tributación Electrónica) at https://sitio.dgi.gob.pa. RUC (Registro Único de Contribuyentes) issuance and all tax returns are processed through SITe or authorized bank collection agents.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a Private Interest Foundation (PIF) incorporated under Ley 25 de 12 de junio de 1995: (i) register the foundation deed with the Registro Público de Panamá (Public Registry) through a licensed attorney/registered agent; (ii) pay the one-time foundation registration fee (USD 350) and the annual flat tax (USD 300, due on or before June 30 each year) using the DGI collection forms (Formulario 100/DGI bank forms); (iii) submit the Aviso de Operación (Notice of Operation) to DGI only if the foundation will conduct Panama-source commercial activity; (iv) apply for an RUC through SITe (Formulario de Inscripción de Contribuyente) if the foundation engages in taxable domestic transactions or wishes to claim ITBMS export zero-rating/credits. For a pure offshore film-licensing PIF (foreign licensees, royalties remitted from abroad, no Panama establishment), RUC registration is not statutorily mandatory; however, voluntary RUC registration facilitates the issuance of export e-invoices and substantiation of the 0% rate. Non-resident founders and beneficiaries are not subject to Panamanian RUC requirements for personal capacity. The local registered agent must confirm identity documents, foundation council appointments, and beneficial ownership data (Ley 254 de 2021) during registration.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Territorial_Scope: The PIF is a distinct separate patrimony (patrimonio autónomo) with legal personality. It is neither an income-tax pass-through nor an ordinary corporation; it is treated as a taxable entity only with respect to Panama-source income. Income derived from the licensing, sub-licensing, or distribution of motion picture copyrights to non-residents, with economic exploitation occurring entirely outside Panama, is outside the scope of Panama's Impuesto Sobre la Renta (ISR). If the PIF engages in Panama-source commercial activity, it is taxed at the standard corporate ISR rate of 25% on net Panama-source profit (and dividend distribution rules apply to distributable profits). The annual flat USD 300 foundation tax is a fiscal obligation independent of income and is not an entity-level income tax.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Panama does not maintain a US-style 'check-the-box' or hybrid-mismatch election regime for entity classification. The PIF's hybrid nature is established by its constitutive deed under Ley 25, which may elect to apply trust-like principles (fiduciary duties, beneficiary rights) without converting the foundation into a corporation. Statutory elections available for tax purposes include: (i) election to remain a non-registered offshore foundation (no RUC) versus voluntary RUC registration for export credit purposes; (ii) election by taxpayers with annual gross revenue below USD 36,000 to use the Régimen Simplificado de Pequeño Contribuyente with reduced ITBMS filing obligations; (iii) election to apply the 0% ITBMS export rate by submitting Form 727 with the export documentation bundle; and (iv) election under the SITe platform to use the 'Factura Electrónica de Exportación' modality for each zero-rated transaction. No separate legal personality election is permitted after incorporation; the deed of foundation fixes the hybrid classification at inception.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: ITBMS (Impuesto de Transferencia de Bienes Muebles y Servicios) — a VAT-type ad valorem tax governed by Articles 1057 et seq. of the Código Fiscal, Ley 8 de 2010, and subsequent amending statutes.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: USD 36,000 (B/. 36,000; Balboa at par with USD) of annual gross sales — economic activities below this threshold may register under the Régimen Simplificado (simplified small-taxpayer regime) with quarterly payments; activities at or above USD 36,000 require full ITBMS registration and monthly Form 727 filings. Pure export transactions and foreign-source service revenues are not considered taxable events and therefore do not count toward the threshold; an exporter whose gross turnover includes only zero-rated foreign transactions is not required to register solely on that volume.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Panama operates a mandatory electronic invoicing system through SITe. Large and medium taxpayers must issue Factura Electrónica (XML) with a DGI-issued digital authorization code and QR stamp; transmission is performed in real time via machine-to-machine API (WSDL/REST) with the DGI validation platform. For exporters, the 'Factura Electrónica de Exportación' is validated online before dispatch, and the invoice must reference the supporting export evidence (contract, remittance certificate, and, for goods, the customs declaration). The clearance mandate includes digital stamping of each authorized document, generation of the 'Código de Autorización de Impresión' for the QR, and archiving of all XML/PDF records for the statutory 5-year period (7 years for large taxpayers). Micro and small taxpayers may use the DGI free web portal; however, credit/refund of input ITBMS is granted only to formal electronic invoicers. Failure to obtain prior electronic authorization invalidates the document and attracts per-invoice fines under Articles 758 and 760 of the Código Fiscal (up to USD 10,000), plus surcharges.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.zero_rating_eligibility: Under Article 1059-A of the Código Fiscal, ITBMS applies at 0% to: (i) exports of tangible goods (with customs departure from Panama); and (ii) services provided to non-resident persons where the use, enjoyment, or economic exploitation occurs entirely outside Panama — this includes the international licensing of motion picture copyrights, sub-licensing of distribution rights, royalty payments from foreign theaters, broadcasters, and streaming platforms, and the rendering of film licensing/administration services to non-resident studios. To qualify, the licensee must be a non-Panamanian tax resident; the licensed copyright must be exploited abroad; the license agreement must be governed by foreign law or executed outside Panama; and the consideration must be settled in foreign currency from abroad. The PIF must issue a Factura Electrónica de Exportación for each royalty invoice and retain the supporting file. Panama-sourced licensing income (i.e., licensing directly for exploitation inside Panama, or services physically rendered in Panama) is subject to the standard 7% ITBMS, regardless of the residence of the licensee.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Panama Customs Export Declaration (Declaración Jurada de Exportación) — required only for physical film prints/DCPs, not for pure intellectual-property licensing transactions
Bill of Lading or Airway Bill (Conocimiento de Embarque / Guía Aérea) — evidence of physical export of goods where applicable

Inward Remittance Certificate (Certificación de Remesa Externa / Certificado de Ingreso de Divisas) issued by a Panamanian licensed bank, evidencing the foreign-currency wire transfer or letter-of-credit settlement within 180 days of the invoice date
Certified copy of the film licensing/sub-licensing agreement with the non-resident licensee, including territory, duration, and royalty schedule
Non-Residence Tax Certificate or beneficial-ownership attestation of the foreign licensee (Certificado de Residencia Fiscal issued by the licensee's jurisdiction)
Factura Electrónica de Exportación validated by the DGI (SITe) with issuance code and QR for the specific zero-rated transaction

Public Registry excerpt of the PIF's foundation deed confirming the PIF's ownership or contractual control over the licensed film copyright and the transaction's authority (foundation council resolution)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The DGI cross-verifies zero-rated export claims against bank remittance data (Sistema de Cuentas Bancarias, SICB) and the beneficial-ownership register (Ley 254 de 2021). Non-compliance with the 180-day foreign-currency repatriation rule, or submission of false or fictitious license documents, exposes the PIF to: (i) immediate clawback of the 0% rate — the underpaid 7% ITBMS is assessed with monthly compounded interest from the original invoice date; (ii) a fraud penalty of up to 100% of the evaded tax (Article 758, Código Fiscal); (iii) administrative fines ranging from USD 5,000 to USD 50,000 for false documentation and the possible cancellation of the exporter's RUC and SITe e-invoicing authorization; and (iv) criminal tax evasion charges under Ley 70 de 2019 and Articles 292-A et seq. of the Código Fiscal, carrying imprisonment of 2 to 5 years for the foundation council members or registered agent involved. The clawback may also be extended to the founder or beneficiaries through the beneficial-ownership disclosure framework, creating joint and several liability for the assessed tax, penalties, and surcharges.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Under Article 1059-A of the Código Fiscal, the ITBMS rate is 0% for: (i) export of goods (customs departure from Panama), and (ii) supply of services to non-resident persons where the use, enjoyment, or economic exploitation occurs wholly outside Panama — this encompasses independent film copyright licensing to foreign distributors, theaters, broadcasters, and streaming platforms. To claim the 0% rate, the licensee must be a non-Panama tax resident; the licensed copyright must be exploited abroad; the license agreement must be executed outside Panama or governed by foreign law; the consideration must be paid from abroad; and the PIF must not engage in any Panama domestic exhibition, distribution, or promotional activity. The exporter must submit the zero-rated export schedule in Form 727 (Declaración de ITBMS) with the supporting documentation bundle. Panama-source licensing (exploitation within Panama) is subject to 7% ITBMS.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Panama Customs Export Declaration (Declaración Jurada de Exportación) — required only for physical film prints/DCPs, not for pure IP licensing
Bill of Lading or Airway Bill (Conocimiento de Embarque / Guía Aérea) — evidence of physical export where applicable
Inward Remittance Certificate (Certificación de Remesa Externa / Certificado de Ingreso de Divisas) from a Panama licensed bank evidencing foreign-currency settlement within 180 days
Film licensing/sub-licensing agreement with the non-resident licensee (territory, duration, royalty, grant of rights)
Non-Residence Tax Certificate or beneficial-ownership attestation of the non-resident licensee
Factura Electrónica de Exportación validated by the DGI (SITe) with issuance code and QR
Public Registry foundation deed excerpt and foundation council resolution authorizing the license
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The DGI Cross-references zero-rated claims against bank remittance data and the beneficial-ownership register. Late or non-repatriation of export proceeds within 180 days triggers: (i) clawback of the 0% benefit with retroactive re-application of the 7% ITBMS plus monthly compound interest; (ii) a fraud penalty of up to 100% of the evaded tax (Art. 758, Código Fiscal); (iii) administrative fines of USD 5,000–50,000 for false documentation and possible cancellation of the exporter's RUC and e-invoicing authorization; and (iv) criminal tax evasion charges under Ley 70 de 2019 (imprisonment of 2–5 years) for willful submission of fictitious license agreements or remittance certificates. The DGI may also issue deficiency assessments against the foundation council and founder through the beneficial-ownership disclosure mechanism.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Panama has no traditional central bank. The Superintendencia de Bancos de Panamá (SBP) is the prudential supervisor of the banking system; Banco Nacional de Panamá acts as fiscal agent of the State; and the Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas (MEF) directs monetary-fiscal coordination in the fully dollarized economy.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Full free convertibility. The US Dollar is legal tender; the Balboa (PAB) is only a notional unit at a fixed 1:1 parity and no national paper currency is issued. Both capital-account and current-account transactions are liberalized; there are no exchange controls, no prior authorizations, and no profit-remittance or distribution restrictions for foundations. Foreign-currency accounts, including EUR and GBP, are freely held; film-royalty and copyright-licensing receipts may be repatriated and converted without SBP approval.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Panama imposes no statutory timeline, mandatory conversion ratio, or export-receipt surrender requirement. Proceeds from film-licensing exports (ISIC 5911) may be retained indefinitely in USD or any freely convertible currency, and treasury mobilisation of such proceeds requires no central-bank notification.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low-to-Medium. Panama has no dedicated Electronic Money Institution (EMI) licensing statute; fintech payment-service providers must be licensed or sandbox-licensed by the SBP and must operate through an SBP-licensed bank. Offshore digital EMIs cannot directly access Panama's USD clearing rails, are not authorised by the SBP, and are routinely declined as treasury counterparties for Private Interest Foundation accounts. Practical use is limited to ancillary local collection wallets (e.g., licensed fintech partnerships) with the master treasury account remaining at a traditional SBP-regulated bank.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Mandatory. SBP due-diligence rules (Acuerdo No. 04-2015, as amended under Ley 23 de 2015) require positive identification of the foundation council, the founder/settlor, the principal beneficiary, and the ultimate beneficial owner. At least one physical or notarised live-video interview with the UBO is required; a Panamanian resident agent (abogado) must also appear before the bank to certify the foundation's legal existence and registered-agent status. Pure remote/paper-only onboarding for a first-time PIF relationship is not available in practice.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Passive, non-trading PIF with broad-purpose clauses and no commercial substance
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarised Acta de Fundación and Reglamento; Registro Público foundation-existence certificate; appointment of the Resident Agent; beneficial-ownership declaration filed under Ley 52 de 2016; council resolution authorising the banking relationship; sworn affirmation that no bearer-share legacy instruments exist.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Film-licensing royalties sourced from multiple foreign distributors, including higher-risk territories
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed film licensing and distribution agreements establishing chain of title; copyright registration certificates; royalty statements from sales agents or collecting societies; invoicing and settlement schedules; counterparty bank references; and fiscal-residence certificates of foreign distributors.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Complex multi-jurisdiction ownership or nominee-council layering
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Updated organisational chart linking settlor, council, protector, and beneficiaries; Panama beneficial-ownership registry extract; statutory declarations from each council member; and a Panamanian legal opinion confirming licit substance and absence of shell-company indicia.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-value inbound wires from non-bank counterparties (production companies, digital platforms, sales agents)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Treasury and transaction-forecast memorandum; counterparty due-diligence pack; underlying ISIC 5911 licensing/royalty contracts; documentary evidence of each expected wire's commercial purpose; and a source-of-funds declaration signed by the counterparty.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident UBO or founder with no Panamanian fiscal nexus
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Valid passport and secondary government-issued ID; tax-residence certificates from all jurisdictions of residence; bank and investment references from the home country; professional curriculum vitae and public-profile corroboration; and a sworn wealth-origin declaration.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound funds are routed by SWIFT MT103 to the PIF's SBP-licensed USD account, with payment reference clearly stating 'Film distribution royalty / copyright license fee under ISIC 5911'. The bank performs OFAC and PEP screening, and the PIF must pre-submit the underlying licensing agreement, a beneficial-ownership attestation, and an invoice or billing letter referencing the PA_PIF client identifier. Founder capital injections are documented as gifts or expendable capital under the foundation deed, with full source-of-funds evidence from the founder's bank. No central-bank approval, FX permit, or declarations are required; however, transactions are subject to SBP transaction-reporting rules for wire activity above USD 10,000 and must be traceable to a documented receivable or contribution.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound settlement is executed in USD via the PIF's local Panamanian account, with onward SWIFT MT103/MT202 transfers cleared through the bank's New York correspondent (e.g., BNY Mellon, Citibank N.A.). Domestic payments use checks and ACH. For film-print delivery, archival services, dubbing/subtitling, and promotional campaigns, the PIF may also use Commercial Letters of Credit under UCP 600 (SWIFT MT700) and Standby Letters of Credit (SWIFT MT760) as performance guarantees for foreign distributor counterparties. Because Panama has no central-bank settlement system, USD clearing is bilateral among SBP-licensed banks; intraday liquidity must be managed through correspondent-account prefunding and daylight credit lines.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable FX forwards in EUR/USD, GBP/USD, and USD/other OECD currencies with tenors aligned to licensing payment milestones
Vanilla FX call and put options for optionality on large lump-sum royalty receipts
Cross-currency interest-rate swaps for multi-year distribution-financing facilities in EUR/USD
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) referencing restricted Latin American currencies (e.g., ARS, VES, PYG) where source-country convertibility is limited
Synthetic USD forward overlays arranged by the Panamanian clearing bank through its New York correspondent window

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Franchise Tax for Private Interest Foundations (Tasa Anual de Fundaciones de Interés Privado) - state continuation fee evidenced by the DGI payment receipt and resident agent endorsement
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI), Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas; collection through Banco Nacional de Panamá via the licensed resident agent
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by 31 May; early-payment rate of USD 250 applies when paid by 31 March; newly registered foundations pay the prorated fee within 60 days of registration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Statutory default interest and surcharges accrue from 1 June; failure to pay for two or more consecutive fiscal years triggers publication of arrears, suspension of registry rights, and eventual administrative strike-off/cancellation before the Registro Público de Panamá

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Ultimate Beneficial Owner (UBO) Sworn Declaration (Declaración Jurada Anual de Beneficiarios Finales)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI), Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas - Régimen de Beneficiarios Finales (electronic beneficial-ownership registry)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by 31 March, reflecting beneficial ownership as of 31 December of the prior year; interim update required within 30 calendar days following any change in the foundation's beneficiaries or foundation council membership
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fines under Executive Decree No. 88 of 2015 and DGI Resolution No. 201-3242 of 2016 (up to USD 1,000 per violation) with continued monthly accrual for persistent non-filing; may restrict registry transactions and materially worsen the foundation's AML risk rating

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Income Tax Return (Declaración Jurada de Impuesto sobre la Renta, Form 210) - required only if the foundation obtains a DGI tax ID (RUC) or realizes Panamanian-source income; a territorial-scope PIF earning solely foreign-source film-licensing royalties is not statutorily required to file
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI), Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For fiscal year ending 31 December: due by 31 March of the following year; a later filing date applies only where the DGI has granted a timely requested extension
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-filing fines under the Panama Tax Code (generally USD 100-USD 500 per return), monthly default interest, and restriction of DGI solvency certificates required for certain banking and public-registry transactions

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No compulsory statutory audit applies to a dormant or foreign-income Private Interest Foundation conducting international film licensing only. A mandatory certified audit arises only if the foundation carries on Panamanian-source commercial activity and, under Law 118 of 2017 and DGI regulations, its gross annual revenue or total assets exceed USD 500,000; audited financial statements must then be submitted to the DGI within the statutory tax-filing period. Banks, licensors, or sub-licensees may contractually require an audit regardless of statutory thresholds.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS (full IFRS or IFRS for SMEs) as adopted in Panama; the foundation may maintain books in US dollars/Balboa and is not required to file financial statements with the Registro Público; internal accounting records must support the territorial-source analysis of film-licensing royalties.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The resident agent must maintain a written and updated UBO file under Law 23 of 2015; an online annual sworn declaration confirming the current ultimate beneficial owners or the absence of changes must be submitted to the DGI by 31 March each year; any change in the foundation's beneficiaries or foundation council composition (the foundation-law equivalent of a shareholding transfer) triggers a fresh declaration within 30 calendar days. The DGI filing remains confidential and is not recorded in the public registry.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Minute Book of Council Resolutions and Proceedings

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 450-1,200 per annum for a licensed resident agent and registered office service in Panama
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 2,000-4,500 per annum for a voluntary certified audit of a simple Private Interest Foundation

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Territorial regime applies: only income with a Panamanian source is subject to corporate income tax. Qualifying foreign-source film licensing royalties earned by a Private Interest Foundation (PIF) are generally outside the Panamanian tax net. No general tax holiday is available for passive IP holding and licensing, but the effective rate on foreign-source licensing income can be 0% under the territorial rule. Domestic Panamanian-source distribution and licensing profits are taxed at 25%.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Formulario 20 – Declaración Jurada de Impuesto sobre la Renta, filed electronically through the Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) T@-Online portal.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The annual income tax return must be filed within three months after the fiscal year-end. For a calendar-year taxpayer, the deadline is 31 March of the following year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxpayer identification: RUC (Registro Único de Contribuyente), foundation name, fiscal year and registered address.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the Panamanian RUC of the PIF. Foreign founders, sponsors and beneficiaries need not be listed on the return, but their identifying data must be available in the foundation AML registry.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Panama-source gross income: revenue derived from activities performed, exploited, or situated in Panama, including film licensing or copyright distribution to Panama-based users.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign-source royalties from non-Panamanian territories or from non-resident licensees must be excluded entirely. Include only receipts sourced to Panama.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductions and costs: expenses directly allocable to production of Panamanian-source income, such as amortization of acquired film rights related to Panamanian exploitation, professional fees, and sub-license fees.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach contracts and invoices. Costs allocable to foreign-source income are not deductible against Panamanian income and should be omitted from the calculation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net taxable income: Panama-source gross income reduced by allocable allowable deductions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If net taxable income is nil, enter zero. Do not offset foreign losses or expenses of the foundation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Corporate income tax at statutory rate: 25% of net taxable income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply 25% only to Panamanian-source taxable income. There is no branch remittance tax on distributions to non-resident beneficiaries.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Credits: advance payments made during the year, withholding tax credits suffered on Panamanian-source income, and tax payments already made.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only Panamanian withholdings and DGI deposit receipts are creditable. Foreign withholding tax credits are not taken because foreign-source income is outside the territorial tax base.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Balance due or overpayment: final tax payable or amount to be credited/refunded.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Any balance due must be paid electronically through DGI by the filing deadline. Overpayments may be applied to future liabilities rather than refunded in most cases.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing imposes an administrative fine of B/. 250–1,000 and a monthly late-filing surcharge of 5% of the tax due, capped at 40% of the tax. Late payment accrues monthly interest at 1.5%, and a 10% enforcement penalty applies if collection proceedings commence. Failure to file after DGI notice can lead to an official assessment with an additional 20–40% overcharge.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% standard dividend withholding tax on distributions paid out of profits already subject to Panamanian corporate income tax. A 20% withholding rate applies to distributions made from profits that have not borne Panama tax, such as foreign-source income or tax-exempt income, unless a specific exemption applies.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Panama's comprehensive tax treaty network is limited. Where an applicable treaty exists, the non-resident recipient must obtain a current Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) from its home country, submit that certificate to the Panamanian paying or withholding agent, and file Form 22 'Certificación de Residencia Fiscal' with the DGI if asked to confirm Panamanian residency of the foundation. The withholding agent applies the reduced rate only after receiving original or certified documents. Excess withholding may be claimed as a refund from DGI within the statutory limitation period (typically five years). For a PIF deriving foreign royalties, the territorial exemption already avoids Panama-source taxation, so treaty application is usually not required.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties paid by a Panamanian taxpayer to a non-resident for film copyright, intellectual property, or licensing rights carry a 12.5% final withholding tax, calculated as 50% deemed net income × 25% corporate rate. Interest paid by a Panamanian taxpayer to non-resident lenders generally carries a 12.5% final withholding tax; certain interest paid by licensed Panamanian banks on foreign deposits is exempt. Treaty rates, where a DTA applies, may be as low as 0–10% depending on the instrument and must be evidenced by a valid TRC.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: B/. 2,000,000 (Panamanian Balboa, 1:1 with the US Dollar) in aggregate annual related-party transactions triggers mandatory Local File and Master File documentation. A separate annual related-party disclosure (Formulario 21) must be filed with DGI when the aggregate threshold is exceeded or when the taxpayer transacts with related parties in no-tax or low-tax jurisdictions.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Panama's Economic Substance Regulations (introduced by Law 254 of 2021 and implementing Decrees) apply to any resident legal entity, including a Private Interest Foundation, that carries on a relevant activity. Film copyright licensing and distribution is a relevant activity for ESR purposes. Such a PIF must maintain a physical office and local staff in Panama, perform core income-generating activity in Panama, and keep records demonstrating board oversight. A PIF that merely holds film royalties abroad without local presence is exposed to ESR penalties and possible loss of tax residence certification.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately omitting Panamanian-source licensing income, inflating deductions, or filing a materially false Formulario 20 return with fabricated contracts, invoices, or beneficial-ownership information.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal tax fraud penalty of one to three times the evaded tax and imprisonment of two to ten years. Administering assessment adds a 25–50% surcharge on understated tax plus monthly interest.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Courts may pierce the foundation's veil where directors knowingly sign false returns. Directors face civil restitution, travel bans, asset freezes and imprisonment for the underlying tax crime.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company and Absence of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating a PIF as a shell vehicle that owns film-licensing rights but has no office, staff, employees, bank account activity or board meetings in Panama, and generates royalty flows solely to obtain tax advantages.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: ESR assessment: annual penalties determined by the DGI, loss of tax residence certificate, real risk of mandatory exchange of information under Panama's tax transparency commitments, and possible cancellation of the foundation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and officers are personally liable for the foundation's substance obligations. Travel bans, disqualification from serving as resident agent, and personal fines may be imposed for willful ESR non-compliance.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML / Foundations Law Breach (Law 25 of 1995 and Law 23 of 2015)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Concealing the ultimate beneficial owner of the foundation, failing to keep the beneficial-ownership register, using the PIF as an unlawful payment-rail or to launder film-licensing proceeds, or failing to appoint the required resident agent.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative fines up to USD 1,000,000 per violation under Law 23 of 2015, cancellation of the PIF registration, and criminal money-laundering penalties of five to ten years imprisonment. The PIF's assets may be frozen and forfeited.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and resident agents have personal exposure to civil restitution, travel bans and imprisonment when they knowingly enable concealed ownership or money-laundering through the foundation.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Licensing film rights to or from related parties at rates outside the arm's length range, failing to file Formulario 21 (related-party disclosure), or failing to prepare and maintain Master File and Local File when aggregate related-party transactions exceed B/. 2,000,000.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: DGI may adjust the taxpayer's income to reflect arm's length pricing, disallow deductions, impose a 10–20% understatement penalty on the additional tax, and accrue interest from the original filing due date.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly sign false TP documentation or approve artificially structured royalty flows may be jointly and severally liable for the resulting tax deficiency and may face tax fraud charges for willful evasion.
